goals.title: Riemann Hypothesis
goals.statement_short: All nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function have real part 1/2.
goals.why_it_matters: Controls the error term in the prime number theorem; Clay Millennium Problem.
goals.known_partial_results: Verified for the first ~3*10^12 zeros (Platt-Trudgian 2021); >40% of zeros on the line (Conrey; later improvements); Guth-Maynard 2024 improved zero-density estimates.
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only: formalize statement-level infrastructure and known zero-free regions; numerics of zeros as a sanity benchmark.

goals.title: P vs NP
goals.statement_short: Is every language verifiable in polynomial time also decidable in polynomial time?
goals.why_it_matters: Central question of complexity theory; Clay Millennium Problem.
goals.known_partial_results: Known barriers: relativization (Baker-Gill-Solovay), natural proofs (Razborov-Rudich), algebrization (Aaronson-Wigderson).
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only: track circuit lower bound literature; formalize barrier theorems as a Lean exercise.

goals.title: Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness
goals.statement_short: Do smooth finite-energy initial data for 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes always yield global smooth solutions (or can blowup occur)?
goals.why_it_matters: Clay Millennium Problem; foundations of fluid mechanics.
goals.known_partial_results: Tao 2016 blowup for an averaged NS; Buckmaster-Vicol non-uniqueness of weak solutions; Chen-Hou computer-assisted blowup for 3D Euler with boundary; 2025 DeepMind/academic work on unstable self-similar singularities via physics-informed networks (reported, partly preprint).
goals.suggested_attack: Follow computer-assisted blowup program (candidate singularity found numerically, then rigorous interval-arithmetic proof); physics-agent monitors.

goals.title: Yang-Mills existence and mass gap
goals.statement_short: Construct a 4D quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 for compact simple gauge group satisfying Wightman-type axioms, and prove a positive mass gap.
goals.why_it_matters: Clay Millennium Problem; would make QCD-type gauge theory mathematically rigorous.
goals.known_partial_results: Rigorous constructions known in 2D and partially 3D; lattice gauge theory results (Chatterjee and others) on Wilson loops and large-N limits; 4D continuum open.
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only; physics-agent tracks lattice/probabilistic approaches.

goals.title: Hodge Conjecture
goals.statement_short: On a projective non-singular complex variety, every rational Hodge class is a rational combination of classes of algebraic cycles.
goals.why_it_matters: Clay Millennium Problem; links topology and algebraic geometry.
goals.known_partial_results: Known for (1,1)-classes (Lefschetz (1,1) theorem) and hence for dim<=3 consequences; false with integer coefficients (Atiyah-Hirzebruch).
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only.

goals.title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture
goals.statement_short: The rank of an elliptic curve over Q equals the order of vanishing of its L-function at s=1 (plus the refined leading-term formula).
goals.why_it_matters: Clay Millennium Problem; governs rational points on elliptic curves.
goals.known_partial_results: Rank 0 and 1 cases known when analytic rank <=1 (Gross-Zagier, Kolyvagin); Bhargava-Shankar: average rank bounded, positive proportion satisfy BSD.
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only; numeric checks via LMFDB are a good data-agent exercise; mathlib elliptic-curve API is growing.

goals.title: Goldbach Conjecture (strong)
goals.statement_short: Every even integer greater than 2 is a sum of two primes.
goals.why_it_matters: Iconic additive prime problem.
goals.known_partial_results: Weak (ternary) Goldbach proved by Helfgott 2013; strong form verified to 4*10^18 (Oliveira e Silva et al.); Chen's theorem (prime + P2).
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only; note Helfgott's ternary proof is a (very large) formalization candidate.

goals.title: Twin Prime Conjecture
goals.statement_short: There are infinitely many primes p with p+2 also prime.
goals.why_it_matters: Paradigm problem for sieve theory.
goals.known_partial_results: Zhang 2013 bounded gaps; Maynard-Tao; Polymath8b: liminf of prime gaps <= 246 (<=6 under Elliott-Halberstam generalization).
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only; formalizing Maynard's sieve bound is a long-term D-style project.

goals.title: Collatz Conjecture
goals.statement_short: Iterating n -> n/2 (even) or 3n+1 (odd) reaches 1 for every positive integer n.
goals.why_it_matters: Famous simple-to-state problem; benchmark for AI hype vs reality.
goals.known_partial_results: Tao 2019: almost all orbits attain almost bounded values; computationally verified to roughly 2^70 range (Barina, ongoing); Collatz-like Busy Beaver 'cryptids' show related undecidability flavour.
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only; do NOT spend compute on brute-force verification.

goals.title: abc Conjecture (status)
goals.statement_short: For every eps>0, only finitely many coprime a+b=c have c > rad(abc)^(1+eps).
goals.why_it_matters: Implies many Diophantine results (e.g. asymptotic FLT, Mordell).
goals.known_partial_results: Mochizuki's IUT proof claim (2012, published PRIMS 2021) is not accepted by most experts after the Scholze-Stix objection; later claims (e.g. K. Joshi 2024) also unresolved; there has been public discussion of Lean formalization of IUT - status uncertain, verify before citing.
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only; literature-agent maintains an honest status note.

goals.title: Union-closed sets conjecture (Frankl)
goals.statement_short: Every finite union-closed family with a nonempty set has an element in at least half of its sets.
goals.why_it_matters: Classic; recent entropy breakthrough shows AI-adjacent info-theoretic methods matter.
goals.known_partial_results: Gilmer 2022 constant fraction; improved to ~0.38 by Alweiss-Huang-Sellke, Chase-Lovett, Sawin, Yu, Cambie; 1/2 still open.
goals.suggested_attack: Formalize the entropy argument (D-style spinoff); search small families for extremal behaviour.

goals.title: Lonely runner conjecture
goals.statement_short: k runners with distinct constant speeds on a unit circle: each runner is at some time at distance >=1/k from all others.
goals.why_it_matters: Connections to view-obstruction, flows in graphs, chromatic numbers of distance graphs.
goals.known_partial_results: Proved up to 7 runners (Barajas-Serra 2008); 2025 preprints reportedly extend to 8, 9 and 10 runners via computer-assisted arguments - verify status.
goals.suggested_attack: Literature check of 2025 preprints; if valid, formalize the finite reduction + certificate in Lean.

goals.title: Hadwiger conjecture
goals.statement_short: Every graph with no K_t minor is (t-1)-colourable.
goals.why_it_matters: Generalizes the four colour theorem.
goals.known_partial_results: Known for t<=6 (Robertson-Seymour-Thomas, uses 4CT); O(t log log t) colouring (Delcourt-Postle 2021).
goals.suggested_attack: Learning; check counterexample-search literature for small cases.
goals.references: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_(graph_theory);Delcourt-Postle 2021 (reducing linear Hadwiger to coloring small dense subgraphs)

goals.title: Erdős-Hajnal conjecture
goals.statement_short: For every graph H there is c>0 such that every H-free graph on n vertices has a clique or independent set of size n^c.
goals.why_it_matters: Central structural Ramsey question.
goals.known_partial_results: Many special cases proved, incl. P5-free graphs (Nguyen-Scott-Seymour 2023).
goals.suggested_attack: Literature-agent maps smallest open H; analogy-agent looks for transferable techniques.

goals.title: Sunflower conjecture
goals.statement_short: Any family of more than C(r)^k sets of size k contains an r-sunflower.
goals.why_it_matters: Applications in circuit complexity and TCS.
goals.known_partial_results: Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang 2019: bound (log k)^k type; refinements by Rao, Bell-Chueluecha-Warnke.
goals.suggested_attack: Formalize ALWZ-Rao proof as a D-side project; search small k,r numerically.

goals.title: Inscribed square problem (Toeplitz)
goals.statement_short: Every Jordan curve in the plane contains four points forming a square.
goals.why_it_matters: Old and elementary; partial results use symplectic topology.
goals.known_partial_results: True for smooth, piecewise-analytic, locally monotone curves; Greene-Lobb 2020 rectangles of any aspect ratio for smooth curves; general continuous case open.
goals.suggested_attack: Learning; formalize the smooth-curve proof as a stretch D target.

goals.title: Jacobian conjecture
goals.statement_short: A polynomial map C^n -> C^n with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant has a polynomial inverse.
goals.why_it_matters: Many false proofs; good test of AI rigor.
goals.known_partial_results: Reduced to cubic homogeneous maps (Bass-Connell-Wright, Yagzhev); true for n=2 up to high degree bounds.
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only; useful red-team benchmark for claimed AI proofs.

goals.title: Erdős-Straus conjecture
goals.statement_short: For every n>=2, 4/n = 1/x+1/y+1/z has a solution in positive integers.
goals.why_it_matters: Classic Egyptian-fraction problem.
goals.known_partial_results: Verified to very large n (~10^17); holds for all n outside few residue classes mod 840; Elsholtz-Tao counting results.
goals.suggested_attack: Low priority: computation alone cannot settle it; formalizing residue-class covering is an easy Lean exercise.

goals.title: Moore graph of degree 57
goals.statement_short: Does a Moore graph (diameter 2, girth 5) with degree 57 and 3250 vertices exist?
goals.why_it_matters: Last unresolved case of Hoffman-Singleton theorem.
goals.known_partial_results: Hoffman-Singleton: degrees 2,3,7,57 only possible; if it exists it is not vertex-transitive (Higman), automorphism group small (Mačaj-Širáň).
goals.suggested_attack: Literature + structured search under assumed automorphisms; very low odds.

goals.title: Unit distance problem: true exponent
goals.statement_short: Determine the growth of the maximum number of unit distances among n points in the plane.
goals.why_it_matters: Erdős 1946 conjecture n^{1+o(1)} was reportedly disproved in May 2026 by an OpenAI model; exponent now open between ~1.014 and 4/3.
goals.known_partial_results: Upper bound O(n^{4/3}) (Spencer-Szemeredi-Trotter); 2026 OpenAI construction beat n^{1+o(1)} by a tiny polynomial factor; Sawin pushed to ~n^{1.014}; Alon-Bloom-Wood gave a human-verified digest (verify exact numbers).
goals.suggested_attack: Read arXiv:2605.20695 and companions; try to push the exponent via construction-agent; formalize digest (see D row).

goals.title: Odd perfect numbers
goals.statement_short: Does an odd perfect number exist?
goals.why_it_matters: One of the oldest open problems.
goals.known_partial_results: Any odd perfect number exceeds 10^1500 (Ochem-Rao 2012) and has many structural constraints (Euler form, >=10 distinct prime factors, etc.).
goals.suggested_attack: Learning; formalize Euler's form theorem as a warm-up if not in mathlib.

goals.title: Inverse Galois problem for M23
goals.statement_short: Is the Mathieu group M23 a Galois group over Q?
goals.why_it_matters: Only sporadic simple group not known to be realized over Q.
goals.known_partial_results: All other sporadic groups realized (mostly via rigidity); M23 resists rigidity methods.
goals.suggested_attack: Literature + computational search of polynomial families (Magma/PARI); low odds.

goals.title: Erdős problems sweep (erdosproblems.com)
goals.statement_short: Systematically triage open problems on erdosproblems.com: literature-resolved, AI-tractable, construction-type, or deep.
goals.why_it_matters: Highest-yield known pipeline for AI-assisted results in 2025-2026; several problems resolved by literature search or AI (e.g. GPT-5.2 Pro + Aristotle).
goals.known_partial_results: Many problems had status changes in 2025-2026 via literature discovery and AI proofs; Epoch AI FrontierMath Erdős benchmark (68 significant open problems as of Aug 2026); community wiki tracks AI contributions.
goals.suggested_attack: literature-agent triages 20 problems/week; lean-agent states them in Lean (cross-check google-deepmind/formal-conjectures); report findings to site maintainers.

goals.title: Formal-conjectures contributions
goals.statement_short: Contribute correct Lean 4 statements of open conjectures (Erdős, OEIS, Wikipedia lists) to the formal-conjectures repository.
goals.why_it_matters: Concrete, reviewable output; mis-stated conjectures are a known failure mode, so careful statements are valued.
goals.known_partial_results: Repository launched by Google DeepMind in 2025 with hundreds of statements; open PRs welcome.
goals.suggested_attack: lean-agent drafts statements; literature-agent checks against source; test against known small cases.

goals.title: Ramsey number R(5,5)
goals.statement_short: Determine R(5,5); currently 43 <= R(5,5) <= 46.
goals.why_it_matters: Most famous small Ramsey number.
goals.known_partial_results: Lower bound 43 (Exoo 1989); upper bound 46 (Angeltveit-McKay 2024, large computation); McKay-Radziszowski conjecture R(5,5)=43.
goals.suggested_attack: Do not attack the upper bound directly; instead study (5,5)-good graphs on 42 vertices and verify catalogue claims.

goals.title: Ramsey number R(3,10)
goals.statement_short: Determine R(3,10); known 40 <= R(3,10) <= 41 (verify latest).
goals.why_it_matters: Smallest open two-colour Ramsey number of form R(3,k); one-step gap.
goals.known_partial_results: Lower bound 40 (Exoo 1989); upper bound improved to 41 by Angeltveit (2023/24 preprint, computer-assisted) - verify.
goals.suggested_attack: SAT/graph-search for triangle-free graphs on 40 vertices with independence number <10; or try to close the upper bound with gluing methods.

goals.title: Multicolour Ramsey R(3,3,3,3)
goals.statement_short: Determine the 4-colour triangle Ramsey number; known 51 <= R(3,3,3,3) <= 62.
goals.why_it_matters: Gap is wide; lower bound via explicit constructions is a natural AI search target.
goals.known_partial_results: Lower 51 (Chung 1973); upper 62 (Fettes-Kramer-Radziszowski 2004).
goals.suggested_attack: construction-agent: search 4-colourings of K_51 without monochromatic triangles (improve to 52 = new result); use Schur-like and cyclic structures.

goals.title: Schur number S(6) bounds
goals.statement_short: Largest n such that {1..n} can be partitioned into 6 sum-free sets; known 536 <= S(6) <= 1836.
goals.why_it_matters: S(5)=160 was settled by a 2PB SAT proof (Heule 2017); S(6) lower bound open to search.
goals.suggested_attack: construction-agent: symmetric/template search to beat 536; also weak Schur numbers.

goals.title: Van der Waerden numbers: new lower bounds
goals.title_he: מספרי ון דר וורדן: חסמים תחתונים
goals.statement_short: Improve lower bounds for unknown W(r,k) (e.g. W(2,7), W(3,5), W(4,4)) by explicit colourings.
goals.why_it_matters: Constructions are checkable certificates; prior records came from structured search (Rabung, cyclic zipping).
goals.known_partial_results: ESH27 Lab 2026-11-11 (L1, makshan-reviewed): 3-colourings certifying W(3,7)>70357 (table: 48811) and W(3,8)>494285 (table: 238400), via Kim's Thm 2.1 (arXiv:2610.32000) with SAT-found polychromatic blocks q=19/43 on Rabung bases; verified by 3 independent checkers. Not found in any accessible source; residual teiku: Xiu-Li-Liang-Xu 2014 unread. Negative results on W(4,4),W(5,4),W(3,5),W(2,7) and 4 more cells. No Lean certificate (size). Prior: exact values known only for few cases; tables by Rabung-Lotts, Monroe, Kim 2026.
goals.suggested_attack: construction-agent: cyclic/power-residue colourings + local search; any new record is publishable as a short note with certificate.

goals.title: Cap sets in F_3^n (sizes and capacity)
goals.statement_short: Find larger cap sets in small dimensions (max size open for n>=7) and improve the asymptotic capacity lower bound.
goals.why_it_matters: Flagship FunSearch result; direct benchmark for our search stack.
goals.known_partial_results: Max size known up to n=6 (112, Potechin 2008); FunSearch found a 512-cap in n=8 and capacity lower bound ~2.2202; upper bound 2.756^n (Ellenberg-Gijswijt).
goals.suggested_attack: Reproduce FunSearch with open models (OpenEvolve-style), then target n=7 lower bound and admissible-set constructions for capacity.

goals.title: Kissing numbers: lower bounds in dims 10-31
goals.statement_short: Find larger kissing configurations in dimensions where exact values are unknown.
goals.why_it_matters: Active AI vs human race 2025-2026 (AlphaEvolve 593 in dim 11; Ganzhinov; PackingStar dims 25-31; Cohn-Li dims 17-21).
goals.known_partial_results: Exact known only in dims 1,2,3,4,8,24; 2025-2026 records changed in dims 10,11,14,17-21,25-31 - pull current table before claiming.
goals.suggested_attack: Check Cohn's table; target dimensions with stale records; certify via exact or rational coordinates.

goals.title: Hadwiger-Nelson problem (chromatic number of the plane)
goals.statement_short: Chromatic number of the plane is in {5,6,7}; find smaller 5-chromatic unit-distance graphs or progress toward 6.
goals.why_it_matters: De Grey 2018 breakthrough came from computer search; Polymath16 found smaller graphs.
goals.known_partial_results: 5 <= chi <= 7 (de Grey 2018); smallest known 5-chromatic unit-distance graph has 509 vertices (Parts 2020); related bounds for plane colourings with restricted tiles.
goals.suggested_attack: SAT-guided search for smaller 5-chromatic UDGs; 6-chromatic would be a major result.

goals.title: Heilbronn triangle problem (small n)
goals.statement_short: Place n points in a unit square/triangle/disk maximizing the minimum triangle area; optimal configurations unknown for most n.
goals.why_it_matters: AlphaEvolve improved some small-n records in 2025; natural continuous optimisation target.
goals.known_partial_results: Optimal known for n<=8 or so in the square; AlphaEvolve reported improved configurations for some cases (see results repo).
goals.suggested_attack: Gradient + evolutionary search; certify with exact arithmetic.

goals.title: Erdős minimum overlap problem
goals.statement_short: Determine the limiting constant M in Erdős's minimum overlap problem (known 0.379005 <= M <= ~0.3809).
goals.why_it_matters: AlphaEvolve improved the upper bound slightly in 2025; step-function optimisation.
goals.known_partial_results: Lower bound 0.379005 (White 2022); upper bound improved by Haugland 2016, then AlphaEvolve 2025 (~0.380924) - verify current value.
goals.suggested_attack: Large-scale step-function optimisation; rigorous verification via exact rationals.

goals.title: Autocorrelation / Sidon-type constants
goals.statement_short: Improve bounds for autoconvolution inequality constants (e.g. sup of f*f for nonnegative f with integral 1).
goals.why_it_matters: Several were improved by AlphaEvolve and follow-ups; easy-to-verify numerical certificates.
goals.known_partial_results: Bounds by Matolcsi-Vinuesa, Cloninger-Steinerberger; 2025 AlphaEvolve improvements on some constants.
goals.suggested_attack: Optimisation over step functions + LP duality for lower bounds.

goals.title: Circle and polygon packing records
goals.statement_short: Improve best-known packings (circles in square, unit hexagons in hexagon, etc.) for specific n.
goals.why_it_matters: Packomania tables; AlphaEvolve beat some records (hexagons n=11,12); clean benchmark.
goals.known_partial_results: Records tracked on Packomania (Specht); optimality proven only for small n.
goals.suggested_attack: Global optimisation + basin hopping; prioritize sizes with old records.

goals.title: Largest sum-free subset constant
goals.statement_short: Every set of n integers has a sum-free subset of size n/3 + f(n); determine growth of f.
goals.why_it_matters: Erdős problem; Bedert 2025 proved f(n) >= c log log n, upper bound much larger.
goals.known_partial_results: Bourgain: (n+2)/3; Bedert 2025: n/3 + c log log n; upper bounds of order o(n) via Eberhard-Green-Manners.
goals.suggested_attack: Literature + construction search for upper-bound examples; formalize Bedert (D row).

goals.title: Sidon sets in [1,N]
goals.statement_short: Maximum Sidon set size in {1..N} is N^{1/2} + O(N^{1/4}); improve the second-order term.
goals.why_it_matters: Erdős prize problem.
goals.known_partial_results: Upper bound N^{1/2}+0.998N^{1/4} (Balogh-Füredi-Roy 2021), later small improvements; lower via Singer/Bose constructions.
goals.suggested_attack: Computational exploration of optimal Sidon sets for moderate N (known tables); look for patterns.

goals.title: Crossing number of K_13 (Hill conjecture)
goals.statement_short: Hill conjecture predicts cr(K_n) = 1/4 floor(n/2)floor((n-1)/2)floor((n-2)/2)floor((n-3)/2); verified for n<=12.
goals.why_it_matters: Next case K_13 is a concrete computational frontier.
goals.known_partial_results: Proved for n<=12 (Pan-Richter 2007); asymptotic lower bounds via flag algebras/SDP (de Klerk et al.).
goals.suggested_attack: SAT/ILP over rotation systems with symmetry; check recent preprints first.

goals.title: Conway's 99-graph problem
goals.statement_short: Does a strongly regular graph srg(99,14,1,2) exist?
goals.why_it_matters: Conway $1000 prize; clean yes/no with a certificate if yes.
goals.known_partial_results: Many structural constraints; no example known.
goals.suggested_attack: Search under assumed automorphism groups; literature-agent collects nonexistence constraints.

goals.title: Hadamard matrix of order 668
goals.statement_short: Construct a Hadamard matrix of order 668 (smallest unknown order).
goals.why_it_matters: Hadamard conjecture; a single construction is a definitive, publishable result.
goals.known_partial_results: Hadamard matrices known for all orders 4k < 668 (order 428 found by Kharaghani-Tayfeh-Rezaie 2005).
goals.suggested_attack: Search Goethals-Seidel/Williamson-type arrays with symmetry assumptions; very hard but certificate-checkable.

goals.title: Turán density of K_4^(3)
goals.statement_short: Determine pi(K_4^(3)); Turán conjectured 5/9.
goals.why_it_matters: Flag-algebra SDP bounds are computational and verifiable.
goals.known_partial_results: Upper bound ~0.5617 via flag algebras (Razborov; Baber-Talbot); many extremal constructions (Brown, Kostochka, Fon-der-Flaass).
goals.suggested_attack: Reproduce flag-algebra SDP; explore new extremal constructions with search.

goals.title: No-three-in-line problem
goals.statement_short: Can 2n points with no three collinear always be placed in an n x n grid for all large n?
goals.why_it_matters: Solutions known up to n=46; conjectured to fail for large n.
goals.known_partial_results: 2n achievable for n<=46 (Flammenkamp); Guy-Kelly heuristic suggests ~c n asymptotically with c<2.
goals.suggested_attack: Extend search to n=47+ with symmetry constraints; certificates are trivially checkable in Lean.

goals.title: Erdős-Szekeres happy ending for hexagon+1 (ES(7))
goals.statement_short: Prove that every 33 points in general position contain a convex heptagon (ES(7)=33, conjectured 2^{n-2}+1).
goals.why_it_matters: ES(6)=17 was proven by computer (Szekeres-Peters 2006); empty hexagon h(6)=30 was SAT-solved and Lean-verified 2024.
goals.known_partial_results: ES(n)=2^{n-2}+1 proven for n<=6; Suk 2017 asymptotic 2^{n+o(n)}.
goals.suggested_attack: Study the SAT encoding used for empty hexagon (Heule-Scheucher) and assess feasibility for ES(7).

goals.title: OEIS conjecture mining
goals.statement_short: Scan OEIS entries containing 'Conjecture:' and triage which are provable, refutable by computation, or already known.
goals.why_it_matters: Large pool of small open statements; good for proving/disproving with AI + Lean.
goals.known_partial_results: Prior automated efforts (e.g. Ramanujan Machine-style conjecture generation, LLM-based OEIS work); many conjectures are easy, some deep.
goals.suggested_attack: Automated pipeline: extract, test numerically to large N, attempt proof; publish batch results.

goals.title: Erdős-Gyárfás conjecture
goals.statement_short: Every graph with minimum degree >=3 contains a cycle whose length is a power of 2.
goals.why_it_matters: Counterexample search is natural for AI; verified for small graphs.
goals.known_partial_results: Holds for claw-free graphs, planar cubic graphs (Heckman-Krakovski); any counterexample has >=17 vertices (and larger bounds for cubic graphs).
goals.suggested_attack: Exhaustive/guided search on cubic graphs; literature check of verification bounds.

goals.title: Snake-in-the-box records
goals.statement_short: Longest induced path (snake) in the hypercube Q_n; exact known up to n=8.
goals.why_it_matters: Long-standing record table improved by heuristic and evolutionary search.
goals.known_partial_results: Exact for n<=8 (n=8 by Östergård-Pettersson 2014); lower bounds for n>=9 improved incrementally.
goals.suggested_attack: Monte-Carlo tree search / evolution; certificates are simple.

goals.title: Busy Beaver BB(6) cryptids
goals.statement_short: Decide halting for remaining 6-state Turing machines; several are Collatz-like 'cryptids'.
goals.why_it_matters: BB(5)=47,176,870 was proved with Coq in 2024 by the bbchallenge collaboration; community is AI-friendly.
goals.known_partial_results: BB(5) settled 2024; BB(6) has huge lower bounds and unresolved machines (e.g. Antihydra).
goals.suggested_attack: Write and formally verify new deciders; join bbchallenge.

goals.title: Spherical codes and covering codes tables
goals.statement_short: Improve best known spherical codes (Sloane tables) and covering/constant-weight code records.
goals.why_it_matters: Large public tables; every improvement is a checkable record.
goals.known_partial_results: Tables by Sloane (spherical codes), Brouwer (constant-weight codes), Kéri (covering codes).
goals.suggested_attack: Optimisation sweeps on stale entries; exact verification.

goals.title: Small Ramsey-type numbers in Lean via SAT certificates (S(4)=44, W(3,3)=27, W(2,4)=35)
goals.title_he: מספרי רמזי קטנים ב-Lean עם תעודות SAT
goals.statement_short: Produce sorry-free Lean 4 proofs of exact small Schur/van der Waerden values, using verified LRAT checking or bv_decide-style tactics.
goals.why_it_matters: Warm-up that builds the SAT->Lean pipeline needed for every C-tier result; check whether already done first.
goals.known_partial_results: ESH27 Lab 2026-11-05 (L3, kernel-only): S(1)=1, S(2)=4, S(3)=13, W(2,3)=9, S(4)>=44, W(3,3)>26, W(2,4)>34. L3 with native_decide trust (Lean.ofReduceBool): W(3,3)=27, W(2,4)=35 via CaDiCaL LRAT + core Lean LRAT checker. Open in Lean: S(4)<=44 (LRAT ~520MB). Results known in literature (Heule 2017 for S(4)); this is formalization, not new math.
goals.suggested_attack: Week 1 literature check; encode; generate LRAT; check in Lean; publish repo + short note.

goals.title: R(4,5)=25 in Lean
goals.statement_short: Formalize R(4,5)=25 (McKay-Radziszowski 1995) in Lean 4.
goals.why_it_matters: Formally verified in HOL4 (Gauthier-Brown 2024); a Lean version would be a strong pipeline demonstration.
goals.known_partial_results: HOL4 proof by Gauthier and Brown 2024 used large SAT computations.
goals.suggested_attack: Reuse the HOL4 decomposition; port certificates; requires serious compute.

goals.title: Formalize recently AI-solved Erdős problems
goals.title_he: פורמליזציה של בעיות ארדש שנפתרו לאחרונה בעזרת AI
goals.statement_short: Pick Erdős problems resolved 2025-2026 (e.g. #728 reported solved by GPT-5.2 Pro, Jan 2026) whose proofs lack a Lean formalization, and formalize them.
goals.why_it_matters: Verification closes the trust gap on AI-claimed results; short proofs, high visibility.
goals.known_partial_results: Several AI solutions were already Lean-checked (e.g. via Harmonic's Aristotle); check the community wiki for which are not.
goals.suggested_attack: literature-agent lists candidates with proof length; lean-agent formalizes the shortest unformalized ones.

goals.title: Unit-distance counterexample (2026) in Lean
goals.statement_short: Formalize the Alon-Bloom-Wood digest of the May 2026 OpenAI construction disproving the n^{1+o(1)} unit-distance conjecture.
goals.why_it_matters: Highest-profile AI math result of 2026; a Lean proof would be widely noticed.
goals.known_partial_results: Human-verified digest exists; uses algebraic number theory that may be partially missing in mathlib - check whether someone has already formalized it.
goals.suggested_attack: Assess mathlib prerequisites first; blueprint; split into lemmas.

goals.title: 5-chromatic unit-distance graph verified in Lean
goals.statement_short: Formally verify that the plane is not 4-colourable via an explicit unit-distance graph (exact coordinates + non-4-colourability certificate).
goals.why_it_matters: Turns de Grey's computer-assisted theorem into a kernel-checked one.
goals.known_partial_results: De Grey 2018 and Polymath16 graphs (smallest known 509 vertices, Parts); unit distances in Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, ...) need exact algebraic arithmetic.
goals.suggested_attack: Encode coordinates in a number field; decide distances by norm computations; SAT certificate via LRAT.

goals.title: Gilmer union-closed bound in Lean
goals.title_he: חסם גילמר לקבוצות סגורות לאיחוד ב-Lean
goals.statement_short: Formalize a constant-fraction bound for Frankl's conjecture (Gilmer 2022 / ~0.38 refinements).
goals.why_it_matters: Entropy infrastructure exists from the PFR project; short, celebrated proof.
goals.known_partial_results: Proof is a few pages; check for existing Lean formalizations before starting.
goals.suggested_attack: Reuse PFR entropy API; aim for the 0.38 constant if feasible.

goals.title: Bedert's sum-free theorem (2025) in Lean
goals.title_he: משפט בדרט על קבוצות חסרות סכום ב-Lean
goals.statement_short: Formalize Bedert's 2025 result that every n-element integer set has a sum-free subset of size n/3 + c log log n.
goals.why_it_matters: Resolves a long-standing Erdős question; fresh, unlikely to be formalized yet.
goals.known_partial_results: Uses Fourier analysis on Z (Littlewood-type L1 norm bounds); mathlib has partial Fourier infrastructure.
goals.suggested_attack: Blueprint first; identify missing analytic lemmas.

goals.title: Cap set bound (Ellenberg-Gijswijt) in mathlib
goals.statement_short: Port the Ellenberg-Gijswijt cap set upper bound to Lean 4 / mathlib.
goals.why_it_matters: Lean 3 formalization exists (Dahmen-Hölzl-Lewis 2019); check whether a Lean 4/mathlib port already landed.
goals.known_partial_results: Lean 3 proof available; polynomial method infrastructure in mathlib.
goals.suggested_attack: If not ported: port and upstream to mathlib; good first mathlib PR.

goals.title: Missing theorems from Freek's 100 list in Lean
goals.statement_short: Formalize items on the '100 theorems' list not yet done in Lean/mathlib.
goals.why_it_matters: Public scoreboard; each item closed is a recognizable contribution.
goals.known_partial_results: Lean community maintains a missing list; remaining items tend to be geometry/analysis-heavy.
goals.suggested_attack: lean-agent picks the item with the best prerequisite coverage; coordinate on Zulip.

goals.title: Kuratowski's theorem in mathlib
goals.statement_short: Formalize planarity and Kuratowski/Wagner theorem in Lean 4.
goals.why_it_matters: Graph planarity is a known gap in mathlib; unlocks many graph results.
goals.known_partial_results: Proved 1930; formalized in other systems (e.g. Isabelle); mathlib planarity API minimal - verify current state.
goals.suggested_attack: Choose combinatorial definition (rotation systems) to avoid topology; blueprint.

goals.title: Sylvester-Gallai theorem
goals.statement_short: Formalize: finitely many non-collinear points in the plane determine an ordinary line (Kelly's proof).
goals.why_it_matters: Short, classical, good warm-up; check mathlib/Archive first.
goals.known_partial_results: Proofs by Kelly, Melchior; Green-Tao on ordinary lines count.
goals.suggested_attack: Kelly's minimal-distance argument in Lean's Euclidean geometry API.

goals.title: Kneser graph chromatic number (Lovász)
goals.statement_short: Formalize chi(KG(n,k)) = n-2k+2 via a combinatorial proof (Matoušek's Tucker-lemma route).
goals.why_it_matters: Gateway to topological combinatorics in Lean.
goals.known_partial_results: Lovász 1978; combinatorial proof by Matoušek 2004; Tucker's lemma has combinatorial proofs.
goals.suggested_attack: Formalize Tucker's lemma combinatorially, then Kneser.

goals.title: Busy Beaver BB(5) proof port to Lean
goals.statement_short: Port (parts of) the Coq proof BB(5)=47,176,870 to Lean 4.
goals.why_it_matters: Cross-system verification of a celebrated 2024 collaborative result.
goals.known_partial_results: Full Coq proof by bbchallenge (2024); some Lean decider work exists in the community - check.
goals.suggested_attack: Port deciders one at a time; reuse certificates.

goals.title: Study & extend the completed FLT formalization
goals.title_he: לימוד והרחבה של פורמליזציית משפט פרמה שהושלמה
goals.statement_short: Take open blueprint nodes in Kevin Buzzard's Lean FLT project.
goals.why_it_matters: Long-term flagship; blueprint nodes are well-scoped units of work.
goals.known_partial_results: Imperial FLT project (Buzzard, since 2024); on 2026-09-04 Anthropic announced a complete Lean formalization of FLT produced by Claude agents (~13M lines, reviewed by Buzzard; Anthropic's own account, no independent replication yet).
goals.suggested_attack: Study the proof's architecture and agent workflow as a template for our pipeline; look for cleanup/upstreaming of lemmas into mathlib.

goals.title: Moving sofa problem (Baek 2024) - verification
goals.statement_short: Baek (2024) claims Gerver's sofa (area ~2.2195) is optimal; formalize or computer-check key lemmas.
goals.why_it_matters: Claimed resolution of a 1966 problem; long proof, verification valuable.
goals.known_partial_results: arXiv preprint ~100+ pages; acceptance status in refereed venue - verify.
goals.suggested_attack: Start by formalizing the problem statement and Gerver's construction area; then pick lemmas.

goals.title: Four colour theorem in Lean
goals.statement_short: Port the Gonthier Coq proof (or a new verified computation) of the four colour theorem to Lean 4.
goals.why_it_matters: Iconic computer-assisted theorem; depends on planarity infrastructure (see Kuratowski row).
goals.known_partial_results: Coq proof complete (Gonthier 2005); Lean efforts reported - check status.
goals.suggested_attack: Long-term; first build planar map API.

goals.title: Bunkbed conjecture counterexample verification
goals.statement_short: Formally verify the 2024 counterexample to the bunkbed conjecture (Gladkov-Pak-Zimin).
goals.why_it_matters: A disproved conjecture whose counterexample needs exact probability bounds - good test of verified computation.
goals.known_partial_results: Counterexample built via Hollom's hypergraph counterexample; probability gap is tiny.
goals.suggested_attack: Assess whether exact rational computation is feasible; else verify the reduction lemmas.

goals.title: 3D Euler/Navier-Stokes computer-assisted blowup
goals.statement_short: Find and rigorously prove finite-time singularities for 3D Euler (no boundary) or related models using numerics + interval arithmetic.
goals.why_it_matters: Concrete pathway toward the Navier-Stokes Millennium problem.
goals.known_partial_results: Chen-Hou 2022/23: rigorous blowup for 3D axisymmetric Euler with boundary (Hou-Luo scenario); 2025 work on unstable self-similar solutions using PINNs (DeepMind + collaborators, preprint).
goals.suggested_attack: Reproduce PINN self-similar profiles for 1D/2D model equations (e.g. Córdoba-Córdoba-Fontelos, Boussinesq); learn interval-arithmetic verification.
goals.references: arXiv:2210.07191;Wang et al. 2025 preprint (discovery of unstable singularities with PINNs);https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navier%E2%80%93Stokes_existence_and_smoothness

goals.title: 3D Ising model: rigorous conformal bootstrap bounds
goals.statement_short: Tighten rigorous bounds on 3D Ising critical exponents using numerical conformal bootstrap (SDP).
goals.why_it_matters: No exact solution of 3D Ising; bootstrap gives most precise exponents; computational and verifiable.
goals.known_partial_results: Kos-Poland-Simmons-Duffin-Vichi islands; precision ~1e-6 for Delta_sigma, Delta_epsilon (2016 onward); conditional on CFT assumptions.
goals.suggested_attack: Run SDPB on mixed-correlator systems; reproduce then extend.

goals.title: Smale's 6th problem: finiteness of central configurations
goals.title_he: הבעיה השישית של סמייל: קונפיגורציות מרכזיות
goals.statement_short: Is the number of relative equilibria (central configurations) of the n-body problem finite for any positive masses?
goals.why_it_matters: Smale problem with an algebraic formulation tractable for computer algebra.
goals.known_partial_results: n=4 proved (Hampton-Moeckel 2006); n=5 for generic masses (Albouy-Kaloshin 2012); n>=6 open.
goals.suggested_attack: Tropical/Gröbner methods for n=5 non-generic or n=6 special masses.

goals.title: Haldane conjecture (spin-1 Heisenberg chain gap)
goals.statement_short: Prove the 1D antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain with integer spin has a spectral gap.
goals.why_it_matters: Nobel-related prediction; math formulation is a spectral gap of an explicit Hamiltonian.
goals.known_partial_results: AKLT model gap proved (1987); numerics strongly support; half-integer spin gapless (Lieb-Schultz-Mattis); finite-size criteria (Knabe, Gosset-Mozgunov) reduce gap to finite computations for some models.
goals.suggested_attack: Try finite-size gap criteria + exact diagonalisation for perturbations of AKLT.
goals.references: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haldane_conjecture;Gosset-Mozgunov 2016 (local gap threshold for frustration-free spin systems)

goals.title: Area law for 2D gapped ground states
goals.statement_short: Do ground states of gapped local Hamiltonians on 2D lattices satisfy an entanglement area law?
goals.why_it_matters: Underpins tensor-network methods; proven in 1D (Hastings).
goals.known_partial_results: 1D proved (Hastings 2007; Arad-Kitaev-Landau-Vazirani); 2D special cases (frustration-free, local TQO) only.
goals.suggested_attack: Literature tracking; low tractability.

goals.title: Maximal quantum violation of Bell inequalities (e.g. I3322)
goals.title_he: הפרה קוונטית מקסימלית של אי-שוויוני בל
goals.statement_short: Compute the maximal quantum value of specific Bell inequalities such as I3322 and decide whether finite dimensions suffice.
goals.why_it_matters: NPA hierarchy gives SDP upper bounds; constructions give lower bounds - ideal for AI search + SDP.
goals.known_partial_results: I3322 max ~0.25087556 approached in high dimensions (Pál-Vértesi 2010); exact value and dimension requirement open; MIP*=RE shows general undecidability.
goals.suggested_attack: Construction-agent searches explicit states/measurements; physics-agent runs high-level NPA bounds.

goals.title: Lieb-Thirring optimal constant conjecture
goals.statement_short: Determine the optimal constant in the Lieb-Thirring inequality for gamma=1 in d=3 (conjectured semiclassical/one-bound-state value).
goals.why_it_matters: Controls stability of matter estimates.
goals.known_partial_results: Frank-Hundertmark-Jex-Nam 2021 best known constant; Frank-Gontier-Lewin 2021 showed the semiclassical conjecture fails for some gamma.
goals.suggested_attack: Numerical optimisation of potentials to search for counterexamples or confirm.

goals.title: Hilbert's 6th problem: kinetic to fluid derivation
goals.statement_short: Rigorously derive Boltzmann and then fluid equations from Newtonian particle dynamics for long times.
goals.why_it_matters: Axiomatization of physics; recent major progress.
goals.known_partial_results: Deng-Hani-Ma 2025 claimed derivation of Boltzmann (long time) and incompressible Navier-Stokes from hard-sphere dynamics - under review.
goals.suggested_attack: Literature-agent tracks; learning only.

goals.title: Self-avoiding walk: square-lattice connective constant and 3D exponents
goals.statement_short: Determine the square-lattice connective constant and rigorously prove critical exponents (e.g. nu=3/4 in 2D).
goals.why_it_matters: Honeycomb mu=sqrt(2+sqrt2) proved (Duminil-Copin-Smirnov 2012); square lattice unknown in closed form.
goals.known_partial_results: Rigorous bounds on mu(Z^2) from enumeration (Jensen, Clisby) and Kesten-type bounds; exponents proven only in d>=5.
goals.suggested_attack: Improve rigorous upper/lower bounds on mu(Z^2) via transfer-matrix computations.

goals.title: Kerr stability and cosmic censorship
goals.statement_short: Prove nonlinear stability of Kerr black holes for all subextremal spins and (weak/strong) cosmic censorship.
goals.why_it_matters: Central problems of mathematical GR.
goals.known_partial_results: Klainerman-Szeftel (2022, with Giorgi) slowly rotating Kerr stability; Christodoulou's genericity results for spherical scalar field; full problem open.
goals.suggested_attack: Learning only.

goals.title: PhysLean contributions
goals.statement_short: Formalize physics results (e.g. Wick's theorem, anomaly cancellation conditions, Lorentz group facts) in the PhysLean project.
goals.why_it_matters: Physics formalization is young; contributions are accessible and visible.
goals.known_partial_results: PhysLean (formerly HepLean, J. Tooby-Smith) has growing library and listed TODO items.
goals.suggested_attack: lean-agent + physics-agent pick TODO items each sprint.

creative_proofs.name: Euclid's infinitude of primes
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Instead of listing primes, assumes a finite list and constructs a number (product+1) none of them divides
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Turn 'infinitely many X' into 'any finite list of X can be extended' and build the witness explicitly
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Template for constructive extension arguments; easy Lean target (Nat.exists_infinite_primes)

creative_proofs.name: Archimedes' Method of mechanical theorems
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Found areas/volumes (e.g. sphere = 2/3 cylinder) by imagined balancing of infinitesimal slices on a lever, then proved them rigorously by exhaustion; text survived only in a palimpsest rediscovered by Heiberg 1906
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Separate discovery from proof: use a heuristic physical model to guess the answer, then prove it with a rigorous method
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should run cheap heuristic 'discovery' models (numerics, physics analogies) before attempting formal proof
creative_proofs.reference: The Method (Archimedes Palimpsest); Heiberg 1906; Netz & Noel, The Archimedes Codex (2007)

creative_proofs.name: Brachistochrone via optics
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Modeled the falling bead as a light ray in a medium of varying density and applied Fermat's least-time principle / Snell's law to get the cycloid
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: A variational problem in one field may already be solved by a principle in another; map the objective to a known extremal principle
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Prompt agents to ask 'what physical system optimizes this same functional?'

creative_proofs.name: Seven Bridges of Königsberg
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Discarded geometry entirely and kept only adjacency; reduced the walk question to vertex-degree parity
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Strip a problem to the minimal structure that matters; the answer often becomes a parity count
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Abstraction step: ask agents to produce the most stripped-down model before searching
creative_proofs.reference: Euler, Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis (1736)

creative_proofs.name: Constructibility of the 17-gon
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Translated a ruler-and-compass question into the algebra of roots of unity and successive quadratic extensions (Gauss periods)
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Change the language: geometric constructibility = field-extension degree questions
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should look for an algebraic encoding of geometric/combinatorial constraints

creative_proofs.name: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Used analysis (L-functions, characters) to prove a purely arithmetic statement
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Import analytic tools (generating functions, Fourier/characters) into discrete problems
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should try generating-function / Fourier encodings for counting problems
creative_proofs.reference: Dirichlet, Abh. Königl. Preuss. Akad. Wiss. (1837)

creative_proofs.name: Galois theory and unsolvability of the quintic
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Replaced the search for formulas with the study of the symmetry group of the roots; solvability by radicals = solvable group
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Attach a symmetry object to the problem and translate the question into a property of that object
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Ask agents: what group/automorphism structure does this object carry?

creative_proofs.name: Cantor's diagonal argument
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Builds an element differing from the n-th listed item at position n, so no list is complete
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: To show no enumeration/function covers everything, diagonalize against an arbitrary candidate
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Reusable template for impossibility/lower-bound proofs; well-supported in Lean (Function.cantor_surjective)

creative_proofs.name: Fifteen puzzle unsolvability
creative_proofs.people: W. W. Johnson; W. E. Story
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Permutation parity plus blank-position parity is an invariant of legal moves, so half of configurations are unreachable
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Find the right invariant: a quantity preserved by every move that distinguishes start from target
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Invariant search is mechanizable: agents can propose candidate invariants and check them on move sets

creative_proofs.name: Dehn invariant and Hilbert's third problem
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Introduced an invariant of polyhedra preserved under scissors-congruence; cube and regular tetrahedron differ, so equal volumes need not be equidecomposable
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Design a new invariant tailored to the allowed operations
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Same as above: invariant design as an explicit agent subtask

creative_proofs.name: Sperner's lemma proof of Brouwer fixed point
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: A combinatorial parity-counting lemma on labeled triangulations yields Brouwer's topological fixed point theorem
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Discretize a continuous problem and use a counting/parity argument, then pass to a limit
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Discretization makes topological statements amenable to finite search and formal proof

creative_proofs.name: Gödel's incompleteness theorems
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Arithmetized syntax (Gödel numbering) so a formula can talk about its own provability
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Encode the meta-level inside the object level, then apply diagonalization
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Foundation for understanding limits of automated provers; formalized in several proof assistants

creative_proofs.name: Mutilated chessboard
creative_proofs.people: Max Black (puzzle); popularized by Gamow & Stern, Golomb
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Coloring argument: each domino covers one black and one white square, but two same-colored corners were removed
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: A coloring/weighting turns an exhaustive search into a one-line counting invariant
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Known benchmark where naive automated search is hard but the human invariant is trivial; a test for agent 'insight'
creative_proofs.reference: Black, Critical Thinking (1946); McCarthy 1964 on ATP difficulty

creative_proofs.name: Erdős probabilistic lower bound for Ramsey numbers
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Showed a random 2-coloring of K_n has no monochromatic K_k with positive probability, proving R(k,k) > 2^(k/2) without constructing a coloring
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Existence by showing a random object works with positive probability
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should try 'pick randomly and compute expectation' when explicit constructions fail

creative_proofs.name: Furstenberg's topological proof of infinitely many primes
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Defined a topology on the integers via arithmetic progressions; finitely many primes would make a non-open set open
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Re-cast a statement in an unexpected structure (topology) where it becomes a short contradiction
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Exploration heuristic: try embedding the problem into a different category and look for contradictions

creative_proofs.name: Four Color Theorem (Appel–Haken)
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Reduced the problem to checking ~1,900 reducible configurations by computer, using discharging to prove unavoidability
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Reduce infinitely many cases to a finite unavoidable set, then let the computer check each
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Model for human-designed reduction + machine-checked cases

creative_proofs.name: Four Color Theorem in Coq
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Fully formalized the (Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas) proof in Coq, including the computational part, using small-scale reflection
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Make brute force trustworthy by running it inside a proof assistant (proof by reflection)
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Direct template: verified decision procedures in Lean (decide / native_decide / certified checkers)

creative_proofs.name: Furstenberg's ergodic proof of Szemerédi's theorem
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Correspondence principle turns density questions on integers into multiple recurrence in measure-preserving systems
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Transfer a combinatorial problem to dynamics where powerful structure theorems exist
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should maintain a 'dictionary' of known correspondences between fields

creative_proofs.name: Marjorie Rice's pentagon tilings
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: A homemaker with no formal training found four new types of convex pentagons that tile the plane using her own notation
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Fresh notation and persistence from outsiders can open closed-looking classifications
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Value of unconventional representations; agents can explore with their own encodings

creative_proofs.name: Mirror symmetry count of rational curves on the quintic
creative_proofs.people: Philip Candelas; Xenia de la Ossa; Paul Green; Linda Parkes
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: String theory duality predicted the numbers of rational curves of every degree on the quintic threefold, far beyond what geometers could compute; later proven (Givental; Lian–Liu–Yau)
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: A duality can convert a hard count into an easy computation on the dual side
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should look for dual formulations where the computation is tractable
creative_proofs.reference: Candelas et al., Nucl. Phys. B 359 (1991)

creative_proofs.name: Monstrous moonshine (Borcherds)
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Proved the Conway–Norton conjecture using vertex operator algebras and the no-ghost theorem from string theory
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Numerical coincidences (196884 = 196883+1) signal a hidden structure worth building
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Numerical pattern matching across tables of constants is an agent-friendly discovery task

creative_proofs.name: Fermat's Last Theorem via modularity
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Linked Fermat solutions to elliptic curves (Frey, Ribet) and proved semistable modularity, so a counterexample would yield an impossible non-modular curve
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Translate the problem into a different conjecture inside a richer theory, then prove that
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Shows value of long reduction chains; Lean formalization project led by Kevin Buzzard is ongoing

creative_proofs.name: Robbins conjecture by automated prover EQP
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: An automated equational theorem prover found a proof that Robbins algebras are Boolean, open since the 1930s
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Some purely equational problems are within reach of uniform search with good heuristics
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Equational reasoning is a strong niche for machine search; precursor to the Equational Theories Project

creative_proofs.name: Kepler conjecture (Hales)
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Reduced sphere packing optimality to a finite but huge set of nonlinear inequalities checked by linear programming and interval arithmetic
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Turn an infinite optimization into finitely many certified numerical checks
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Interval arithmetic + LP certificates are reusable machine-checkable proof components

creative_proofs.name: Flyspeck: formal proof of Kepler
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: After referees could not fully verify the computer proof, the team formalized it in HOL Light and Isabelle
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: When human review is the bottleneck, formal verification is the way to close the proof
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Exact motivation for our Lean pipeline: formalize computer-assisted proofs
creative_proofs.reference: Hales et al., Forum of Math, Pi 5 (2017)

creative_proofs.name: Perelman's proof of the Poincaré conjecture
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Used Ricci flow (a heat-like PDE on metrics) with surgery; introduced an entropy-like monotone functional inspired by statistical mechanics
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Evolve the object with a flow that smooths it, and find a monotone quantity controlling the flow
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Look for monotone functionals/potential functions along a process

creative_proofs.name: Dvir's finite field Kakeya
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: A low-degree polynomial vanishing on a Kakeya set must vanish everywhere, giving a near-sharp bound in a short proof
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Find a low-degree polynomial vanishing on the set and use degree counting to get a contradiction
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Polynomial-method templates are short and very suitable for formalization

creative_proofs.name: Zhang's bounded gaps between primes
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: A little-known lecturer outside the research mainstream proved infinitely many prime gaps below 70 million by refining GPY sieve with a smooth-moduli equidistribution estimate
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Small technical improvements on a near-miss method can break a barrier
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should scan 'almost-works' methods for the missing estimate

creative_proofs.name: Maynard–Tao multidimensional sieve
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Changed the sieve weights to multidimensional ones, getting gaps ≤ 600 with a simpler argument that avoided Zhang's hardest step
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: A better choice of auxiliary object (weights) can make the hard part unnecessary
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Optimization over auxiliary functions is a numerical task agents can do

creative_proofs.name: Polymath8: bounded gaps reduced to 246
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Open online collaboration rapidly optimized Zhang's and Maynard's bounds down to 246
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Many small parallel improvements on a modular argument compound quickly
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Model for multi-agent work: shared blueprint, modular sub-bounds, public log

creative_proofs.name: Polymath1: density Hales–Jewett
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: First Polymath: open blog collaboration found a new elementary combinatorial proof of DHJ(3) in weeks
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Publicly decompose a problem into small comments; fast feedback beats lone deep work
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Template for agent swarms with shared notes and frequent small contributions

creative_proofs.name: Erdős discrepancy problem
creative_proofs.people: Terence Tao (after Polymath5; SAT case by Konev & Lisitsa 2014)
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: SAT showed discrepancy 2 sequences have length ≤1160; Tao's full proof used an entropy decrement argument and a reduction to a form of the Elliott conjecture suggested by a blog comment
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Use computation to probe small cases, then a bridge to analytic number theory for the general case
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Combine SAT experiments with human/AI conceptual reduction
creative_proofs.reference: Tao, Discrete Analysis 2016:1; Konev & Lisitsa, SAT 2014

creative_proofs.name: Boolean Pythagorean triples
creative_proofs.people: Marijn Heule; Oliver Kullmann; Victor Marek
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Showed 1..7824 can be 2-colored with no monochromatic Pythagorean triple but 1..7825 cannot, via cube-and-conquer SAT; certificate ~200 TB
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Encode as SAT, split with cube-and-conquer, and emit a checkable DRAT proof
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Direct playbook: SAT encoding + verified proof checker (e.g. cake_lpr) + Lean bridge

creative_proofs.name: Schur number five
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Proved S(5)=160 by SAT with symmetry breaking; proof certificate ~2 petabytes, verified by a formally verified checker
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Symmetry breaking and verified checkers make enormous searches credible
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should exploit symmetry before brute force

creative_proofs.name: Cap set problem via polynomial method
creative_proofs.people: Ernie Croot; Vsevolod Lev; Péter Pál Pach; Jordan Ellenberg; Dion Gijswijt
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Croot–Lev–Pach's slice-rank-type polynomial argument for Z_4^n was adapted within weeks by Ellenberg–Gijswijt to F_3^n, giving an exponential improvement in a 3-page proof
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: When a new technique appears, immediately test it on neighboring problems
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should port a new trick to every related open problem
creative_proofs.reference: Ellenberg & Gijswijt, Annals 185 (2017); Croot, Lev & Pach, Annals 185 (2017)

creative_proofs.name: Viazovska's sphere packing in dimension 8 (and 24)
creative_proofs.people: Maryna Viazovska; with Cohn, Kumar, Miller, Radchenko for dim 24
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Constructed the 'magic function' required by the Cohn–Elkies LP bound using modular forms
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Reduce optimality to existence of an auxiliary function, then build it from a rich special-function theory
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Searching for certificate functions (with numerics guiding) is a promising AI task
creative_proofs.reference: Viazovska, Annals 185 (2017); Cohn et al., Annals 185 (2017)

creative_proofs.name: Chromatic number of the plane ≥ 5
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: A biologist built a 1581-vertex unit-distance graph needing 5 colors, verified by SAT; Polymath16 then shrank the graph
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Outsider builds a big explicit witness; computers verify; community optimizes
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents can generate large witnesses and hand them to SAT for checking

creative_proofs.name: Sensitivity conjecture
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Two-page proof via a signed adjacency matrix of the hypercube and Cauchy interlacing, after ~30 years
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Look for a clever linear-algebra encoding (signed matrices, spectra) of a combinatorial quantity
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Short proofs exist for hard problems; agents should try spectral encodings

creative_proofs.name: Keller's conjecture in dimension 7
creative_proofs.people: Joshua Brakensiek; Marijn Heule; John Mackey; David Narváez
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Resolved the last open dimension (true in dim 7) by reducing to clique existence in Keller graphs and solving with SAT plus symmetry breaking
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Combine structural reductions with SAT and a verified certificate
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Another SAT + verified-checker template

creative_proofs.name: Kaplansky unit conjecture counterexample
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Encoded existence of a nontrivial unit in a group ring of the Hantzsche–Wendt group as SAT; solver found it
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Semi-decidable 'find a counterexample' problems in algebra can be SAT-encoded
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents should encode bounded-support counterexample searches as SAT

creative_proofs.name: Machine learning guiding knot theory and representation theory
creative_proofs.people: Alex Davies et al. (DeepMind); Marc Lackenby; Geordie Williamson; András Juhász
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Supervised learning plus attribution found that the knot signature relates to geometric invariants (natural slope), leading to a proven theorem; also guided progress on combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Train a model to predict invariant A from B, use saliency to find which features matter, then let humans prove the relation
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Concrete pipeline: data generation -> prediction -> attribution -> conjecture -> proof

creative_proofs.name: Ramanujan Machine
creative_proofs.people: Gal Raayoni; Ido Kaminer et al.
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Automated search over continued fraction forms discovered new conjectured formulas for constants like e, pi, Catalan's constant
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Mass numerical search for identities, followed by proof attempts of survivors
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Cheap high-precision numerics as conjecture generator for agents

creative_proofs.name: Constructions in combinatorics via neural networks
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Used reinforcement learning (cross-entropy method) to find counterexamples to several published graph-theory conjectures
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Turn 'disprove conjecture' into maximizing a score that is positive iff counterexample
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Directly reusable: write a score function, run RL/evolutionary search

creative_proofs.name: Heesch number 6
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Found a polyform with Heesch number 6, the highest known, extending computer searches started by Casey Mann
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Systematic computer search over shape families finds record witnesses
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Record-hunting tasks are well suited to search agents

creative_proofs.name: Liquid Tensor Experiment
creative_proofs.people: Peter Scholze (challenge); Johan Commelin et al. (Lean community)
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Scholze asked for a formal check of a key theorem he was unsure about; Lean community verified it (main part 2021, completed 2022), clarifying the proof along the way
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Formalization as a tool for the author's own confidence and for simplifying a proof
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Shows Lean + blueprint can handle cutting-edge abstract math
creative_proofs.reference: Scholze, Xena blog Dec 2020; Commelin et al., github.com/leanprover-community/lean-liquid

creative_proofs.name: AlphaTensor matrix multiplication
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Framed finding matrix multiplication algorithms as a single-player game of tensor decomposition; found 47-multiplication 4x4 algorithm over GF(2)
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Reformulate algorithm discovery as a game with a verifiable score and use RL
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: The output is a certificate (a decomposition) that is trivially checkable

creative_proofs.name: PFR conjecture and its Lean formalization
creative_proofs.people: Timothy Gowers; Ben Green; Freddie Manners; Terence Tao
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Proved Marton's polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture over F_2 using entropy methods; a crowd formalization in Lean with a blueprint finished in about three weeks
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Blueprint (dependency graph of lemmas) lets many contributors formalize in parallel
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Direct model for our agents: blueprint + Lean + parallel lemma assignment
creative_proofs.reference: Gowers et al., arXiv:2311.05762; Tao blog Dec 2023

creative_proofs.name: The einstein 'hat' aperiodic monotile
creative_proofs.people: David Smith; Joseph Samuel Myers; Craig S. Kaplan; Chaim Goodman-Strauss
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: A hobbyist found the shape by experimenting with software; proofs used computer-assisted combinatorics and a geometric incommensurability argument; followed by the chiral 'spectre'
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Exploration by play with good tools finds candidates; experts then prove
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents can run open-ended exploration with visual/software tools and flag anomalies
creative_proofs.reference: Smith et al., Combinatorial Theory 4 (2024), arXiv:2303.10798

creative_proofs.name: FunSearch cap sets
creative_proofs.people: Bernardino Romera-Paredes et al. (DeepMind); Jordan Ellenberg
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: LLM evolved programs (not objects) that generate cap sets, finding a size-512 cap set in dimension 8, larger than previously known
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Search over programs that construct objects; programs are interpretable and generalize
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Core playbook: LLM proposes code, evaluator scores, evolutionary loop

creative_proofs.name: AlphaGeometry
creative_proofs.people: Trieu Trinh; Yuhuai Wu; Quoc Le; He He; Thang Luong
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Neuro-symbolic: symbolic deduction engine plus a language model trained on synthetic data that proposes auxiliary constructions; solved 25 of 30 IMO geometry problems
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Let the model propose creative auxiliary objects, let a symbolic engine do the deductions
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Split creativity (LLM) from verification (symbolic engine)

creative_proofs.name: Empty hexagon theorem
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Proved every set of 30 points in general position contains an empty convex hexagon via SAT, with the encoding itself verified in Lean
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Verify both the SAT certificate and the encoding (the weakest link) formally
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Exact template for SAT + Lean integration
creative_proofs.reference: Heule & Scheucher, TACAS 2024; Subercaseaux et al., ITP 2024 (Lean verification)

creative_proofs.name: AlphaProof at IMO 2024
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: RL agent trained on millions of auto-formalized problems produced Lean proofs for 4 of 6 IMO 2024 problems (silver-medal level)
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Train by self-play in a formal system: the proof checker is the reward signal
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Lean as a reward function is our core architecture
creative_proofs.reference: DeepMind blog July 2024; Hubert et al., Nature (2025)

creative_proofs.name: Busy Beaver BB(5)
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Online collaboration (many amateurs) classified all 5-state 2-symbol Turing machines and proved BB(5) = 47,176,870 with a Coq proof
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Crowdsourced deciders + formal verification can settle massive case analyses
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Combining many heuristic deciders, each proved correct, is a scalable agent pattern

creative_proofs.name: Equational Theories Project
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Settled all ~22 million implications between 4694 magma laws using humans, ATPs, SAT/countermodel finders and Lean verification
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Massive uniform micro-problems are ideal for a mixed human+automation pipeline with Lean as the final arbiter
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Closest existing analogue of an ESH27 swarm

creative_proofs.name: Kakeya conjecture in R^3
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Proved Kakeya sets in R^3 have Hausdorff dimension 3 via multiscale induction on 'sticky' vs non-sticky configurations
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Split into structured vs unstructured cases and induct across scales
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Case decomposition by structure is a strategy agents can propose explicitly

creative_proofs.name: AlphaEvolve: 4x4 complex matrix multiplication and kissing number
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: LLM-driven evolutionary coding agent found a 48-multiplication algorithm for 4x4 complex matrices and a 593-sphere configuration improving the kissing number lower bound in 11 dimensions
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Evolve code with an automatic evaluator; works for any problem with a scoreable construction
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Directly reusable loop for bound-improvement tasks
creative_proofs.reference: DeepMind, AlphaEvolve white paper May 2025; arXiv:2506.13131

creative_proofs.name: Erdős problems and LLM-assisted literature search
creative_proofs.people: Users of erdosproblems.com; Thomas Bloom; Terence Tao
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Oct 2025 claims that GPT-5 'solved' Erdős problems turned out to be LLM literature search finding existing solutions to problems listed as open
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Before attacking a problem, have an AI search the literature: many 'open' problems are already solved
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Mandatory first step for agents: literature search, then claim nothing without checking

creative_proofs.name: Erdős problem #728 solved by AI
creative_proofs.people: Kevin Barreto; GPT-5.2 Pro; Harmonic's Aristotle
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Informal argument by an LLM was formalized in Lean by Aristotle; considered among the first autonomous AI solutions of an Erdős problem (after interpretation of the statement was clarified)
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: LLM proposes informal proof, formal agent verifies; statement interpretation must be fixed precisely
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Exactly our pipeline: informal reasoning -> Lean -> human audit of statement

creative_proofs.name: Noperthedron: polyhedron without Rupert's property
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Constructed a convex polyhedron (90 vertices) and proved it cannot pass through itself, combining theory with a large computer search over orientations
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: Theory reduces a continuous parameter space to a finite grid; computation covers the grid
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Pattern: Lipschitz/error bounds turn continuous search into a finite certified search

creative_proofs.name: Proofs without words
creative_proofs.what_was_creative: Identities such as sum of odd numbers = n^2 shown by a single picture or bijection
creative_proofs.reusable_lesson: A bijection or picture often explains why an identity holds; turn it into a combinatorial proof
creative_proofs.ai_relevance: Agents can search for bijective proofs, which often formalize cleanly

news.title: ESH27 Lab יוצאת לדרך: מחקר מתמטי פתוח, עם בינה מלאכותית ובאימות פורמלי
news.excerpt: היום אנחנו פותחים את ESH27 Lab: מעבדה שבוחרת בעיות פתוחות במתמטיקה ובפיזיקה תיאורטית, תוקפת אותן עם סוכני AI, ומאמתת כל טענה ב-Lean 4 לפני שהיא נקראת „מוכחת”.
news.html:
היום אנחנו פותחים את ESH27 Lab: מעבדה שבוחרת בעיות פתוחות במתמטיקה ובפיזיקה תיאורטית, תוקפת אותן עם סוכני בינה מלאכותית, ומאמתת כל טענה ב-Lean 4 לפני שהיא נקראת „מוכחת”. הכול נעשה בגלוי: מה ניסינו, מה עבד, ובעיקר מה לא עבד.

נתחיל במה שחשוב לומר כבר בשורה הראשונה: לא הוכחנו עדיין שום דבר חדש. הכתבה הזאת היא הודעת פתיחה, לא הודעה על פריצת דרך.

המשימה

לא הקמנו עוד אתר שמסקר את מה שאחרים עושים עם AI במתמטיקה. אנחנו רוצים להפוך בעצמנו לחוקרים, עם הבינה המלאכותית ובזכותה. השיטה פשוטה לתיאור וקשה לביצוע:

  1. בוחרים מטרה מתוך בנק המטרות.
  2. קוראים את הספרות: מה ידוע, מה נוסה, איפה זה נתקע.
  3. מנסחים את הטענה ב-Lean 4, ובודקים עם בני אדם שהניסוח באמת אומר את מה שהבעיה אומרת.
  4. תוקפים: סוכני AI מחפשים דוגמאות, מריצים ניסויים, כותבים טיוטות הוכחה ומפרקים את הבעיה ללמות.
  5. מאמתים: בודק ההוכחות של Lean מכריע, בלי sorry ובלי אקסיומות חדשות.
  6. מפרסמים כאן, ב-S27 News וביומן ההתקדמות של המעבדה.

כנות היא המותג: רמות טענה L0–L4

בעידן שבו מודל שפה יכול לכתוב „הוכחה” משכנעת ושגויה בתוך שניות, האמינות היא המשאב הכי יקר. לכן כל רשומה אצלנו מסומנת ברמת טענה:

  • L0, רעיון: השערה, אינטואיציה או כיוון שעוד לא נבדק.
  • L1, ראיה חישובית: ניסויים או חיפוש מחשב תומכים בטענה, אבל זו לא הוכחה.
  • L2, טיוטת הוכחה: טיעון בשפה טבעית, של אדם או של AI, שנקרא ונבדק בעין. עלולות להיות בו טעויות.
  • L3, מאומת ב-Lean: הוכחה פורמלית מלאה שעברה את בודק ההוכחות, לניסוח שנבדק כנאמן לבעיה.
  • L4, מאומת ונבדק: כמו L3, וגם ביקורת עמיתים חיצונית, פרסום או קבלה ל-Mathlib.

את המילה „הוכחנו” נשתמש רק מרמה L3 ומעלה. כל דבר מתחת לזה ייקרא בשמו: רעיון, ראיה או טיוטה.

חשוב לזכור גם את הגבול של L3: Lean מאמת שההוכחה נכונה עבור הניסוח שנכתב. אם הניסוח עצמו לא נאמן לבעיה, האימות לא שווה הרבה. לכן בדיקת הניסוח היא שלב בפני עצמו.

בנק המטרות

בלב המעבדה יש בנק מטרות פתוח. כל מטרה מקבלת דרגה:

  • A, ירייה לירח: בעיות ענק. לא מבטיחים לפתור; לומדים, מפרקים ומתעדים.
  • B, פתוחות ומפורסמות: בעיות ידועות שיש בהן מקרים פרטיים ותתי-שאלות שאפשר לתקוף.
  • C, ברות-השגה: יעדים שבהם חיפוש בעזרת AI ואימות פורמלי יכולים להביא תוצאה אמיתית.
  • D, פורמליזציה: משפטים ידועים שעוד לא נוסחו ב-Lean. תשתית שכולם נהנים ממנה.
  • P, פיזיקה תיאורטית: שאלות בפיזיקה מתמטית, מודלי צעצוע וניסוח מדויק של הגדרות.

לכל מטרה מצורפת הערכה כנה: עד כמה AI באמת יכול לעזור בה, ועד כמה הניסוח הפורמלי מוכן. אחוזי ההתקדמות באתר מודדים עבודה שנעשתה, לא קרבה להוכחה. ציפייה ריאלית היא שרוב ההתקדמות האמיתית תגיע מדרגות C ו-D, ושבדרגה A נלמד הרבה ונפתור מעט.

מה AI כבר עשה במתמטיקה

אנחנו לא מתחילים מאפס. בשנים האחרונות קרו כמה דברים שמראים שהכיוון אמיתי:

  • FunSearch (Google DeepMind, 2023) שילב מודל שפה עם מעריך אוטומטי, ומצא קונסטרוקציות חדשות בבעיית ה-cap set, יותר טובות מאלה שהיו ידועות עד אז בממדים מסוימים. הלקח: כשאפשר לבדוק פתרון אוטומטית, חיפוש מונחה-מודל יכול לגלות דברים חדשים.
  • AlphaProof (Google DeepMind, 2024), יחד עם AlphaGeometry 2, הגיע לרמה של מדליית כסף באולימפיאדה הבינלאומית במתמטיקה. AlphaProof כתב את הוכחותיו ב-Lean, כך שהן נבדקו באופן פורמלי. ב-2025 כבר דווח על מערכות שהגיעו לרמת מדליית זהב באולימפיאדה.
  • AlphaEvolve (Google DeepMind, 2025), סוכן קוד אבולוציוני, שיפר חסמים ידועים בכמה בעיות פתוחות באנליזה, בגאומטריה ובקומבינטוריקה, ומצא אלגוריתם לכפל מטריצות 4×4 מרוכבות בפחות פעולות כפל מבעבר.
  • בעיות ארדש: כלי AI עזרו לאתר בספרות פתרונות שכבר היו קיימים לבעיות שנרשמו כפתוחות באתר בעיות ארדש, ובמקרים מסוימים גם תרמו לפתרונות חדשים. הפרשה הזאת לימדה גם לקח חשוב על זהירות: „מצאנו פתרון שכבר קיים בספרות” ו„פתרנו בעיה פתוחה” הן שתי טענות שונות מאוד.
  • פרויקטי פורמליזציה שיתופיים, כמו Mathlib ופרויקטים בהובלת מתמטיקאים מובילים, הראו שבני אדם, מחשבים ו-AI יכולים לבנות יחד מתמטיקה מאומתת בהיקף גדול.

המשותף לכל ההצלחות האלה: מנגנון אימות חיצוני. מעריך שמודד, או בודק הוכחות שמכריע. זה בדיוק הבסיס שעליו אנחנו בונים.

גשרי חוכמה

יש במעבדה גם פינה אחרת, שקטה יותר: גשרי חוכמה. הגמרא בנתה במשך דורות שיטה של קושיה ותירוץ, שמזכירה מאוד חיפוש הוכחה והפרכה. ספר יצירה מונה צירופים של אותיות, ובבסיסו עומדת קומבינטוריקה. לוחות חימר בבליים, כמו Plimpton 322, מתעדים שלשות פיתגוריות כבר לפני כ-3,800 שנה.

אנחנו מתייחסים לגשרים האלה כאל השראה, מטפורה וכלי הוראה, לא כאל ראיה מתמטית. הם לא מחליפים הוכחה, ולא נציג אותם ככאלה. הם כן מזכירים לנו שהשאלה „איך יודעים שמשהו נכון?” מלווה את האנושות הרבה לפני שהיו מחשבים.
